A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from XLIP to MMCLIP. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot classification, fine-tuning and masking-ablation results in Tables I–IV and Figures 5–7.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 6–8.

M1.justification: XLIP is renamed MMCLIP. The encoders, three-way AttMIM masking, ScispaCy-based EntMLM, training losses, warm-up procedure and handling of paired/unpaired data remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use MIMIC-CXR and PadChest for pretraining and retain evaluation on CheXpert, PadChest, Pneumonia, COVIDx and Xray14. The new dataset appendix documents existing coverage rather than introducing an additional evaluated dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: Table I/Table 1 retains ConVIRT, GLORIA, BioViL, BioViL-T, CheXzero and MedKlip. Table II/Table 2 retains CheXzero and MedKlip. The fine-tuning and masking-ablation comparator sets also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated training settings, metrics, fine-tuning fractions and 2,200-pair ablation validation set remain unchanged. Appendix A–B newly discloses dataset splits and test-set details without explicitly revising existing protocols; these additions belong to D1.

E4.justification: Both retain the warm-up, individual attention-strategy and text-masking ablations, mask-ratio analyses, unpaired-data comparison and masking example. The former appendix masking diagram moves into the main text without adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version adds seeds, repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals or significance tests. The description of ensembling six parameter configurations is retained and does not constitute uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All table values and plotted results are retained. For example, CheXpert AUC remains 90.53, or 91.45 with ensembling, and AUC across 173 unseen PadChest classes remains 70.00. The fine-tuning chart changes only the method name in its legend.

T1.justification: The attention, masking and loss definitions in Equations 1–16 and the alignment objective remain mathematically unchanged. No assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are added.

C1.justification: Both claim a unified AttMIM/EntMLM framework, support for unpaired images through disease prompts, and state-of-the-art classification performance on five datasets. The expanded abstract explains an existing component without changing the contribution claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly explains that PadChest is used as image-only data because its reports are in Spanish. This adds a specific qualification concerning data use; interpretations of the results and masking mechanisms otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 refers to dataset details that its appendix does not provide. v3 adds Appendix A–B covering dataset sizes and labels, CheXpert’s 500-image test set, COVIDx/Pneumonia/Xray14 splits and patient-level separation for Xray14. This substantially expands reproducibility documentation. Both versions still describe code release as forthcoming.

R1.justification: The same 53 cited works and substantive comparisons with prior research are retained. Expanded bibliographic metadata, including the Thin-Thick Adapter entry, does not introduce a different cited work or research position.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Limited edits rename the framework, expand the abstract’s explanation of EntMLM, update author information and introduce dataset appendix sections before the references.

P2.justification: The IEEE presentation is replaced by ACM styling, with extensive typography, caption and layout changes. Appendix Figure 8 becomes main-text Figure 3; the full-width fine-tuning chart becomes a smaller single-column Figure 6, and sensitivity plots are restacked. Table 3 incorrectly acquires a PadChest caption despite retaining the CheXpert ablation.

improvement.justification: The new dataset appendix fills a concrete documentation gap, making the existing experiments easier to assess and reproduce. This provides a limited net improvement despite the incorrect Table 3 caption and reduced plot legibility. The method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
